properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"I searched if there is an equivalent to a rest open api spec or doc and the answer was not really, but I did find: https://blogs.cisco.com/developer/beyond-the-protocol-applying-api-engineering-practices-to-mcp-servers - I think the flo2 project will need both."*

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

═══ WHAT IS AND IS NOT MISSING, STATED CAREFULLY ═══

MCP is **not** undescribed. Every tool carries a JSON Schema for its inputs, and `tools/list` returns names, descriptions and those schemas — reflow2 leans on it hard, which is why `describe_schema` and `find_tools` can work at all.

**What has no standard is everything OpenAPI carries AROUND the schema:** a versioned document you can diff between releases, deprecation markers, an error taxonomy, worked examples, and a contract a consumer can test against without calling the live server. The Cisco piece Anthony found is about exactly that gap — applying API engineering practice to a protocol that shipped without it.

⭐ **AND THAT IS THE SHAPE OF VOCABULARY REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS.** `cap:interface-spec` — *"A published contract says what a consumer must agree with"*. `cap:a-published-contract-says-what-two-systems-must-agree-on` — a contract is *asked which of the agreement axes it never filled in*. `cap:a-published-contract-is-asked-for-its-evidence`. `export_surface` / `mirror_surface` / `cap:seam-incompatibility` — *say when two linked designs disagree at a boundary*. **reflow2 was built to describe contracts between systems; MCP is a contract between systems with no description standard.** The adjacency is real and nobody has written it down.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) Notice the adjacency and do nothing.** Record it, leave it. ⚠️ Counter: it is genuinely the strongest unclaimed product idea in this brainstorm, and unrecorded adjacency is how the 40 never-called tools happened.

**(b) reflow2 DESCRIBES its own MCP surface as Interfaces in its own graph.** `ifc:mcp-tools` and `ifc:mcp-tools-http` already exist as nodes — this would mean giving them real specs, so reflow2's tool surface has a versioned, diffable contract the way it asks every consumer's design to. ⚠️ Counter: **that is self-hosting, and self-hosting is not the product** (`rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself`). It would prove the shape and serve nobody else directly. It is also close to `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches`, which says that lag is the mechanism rather than a failure.

**(c) reflow2 offers a general capability: DESCRIBE ANY MCP SERVER'S CONTRACT.** Point it at a server, read `tools/list`, and record the surface as Interfaces with specs — so a team can diff their MCP surface between releases, mark deprecations, and get told when a consumer's expectation no longer matches. ⚠️ Counter, and it is the serious one: **this is a different product.** reflow2 is a design brain for systems, not an API-governance tool for MCP servers, and the `dec:idea-is-there-a-lightweight-task-capture-below-the-increment-grain` objection applies with force — every step toward being good at a neighbouring category is a step toward being bad at this one. Anthony's own anti-over-engineering instinct is the strongest argument against.

**(d) ⭐ TREAT IT AS A SEAM QUESTION, WHICH IS GROUND REFLOW2 ALREADY OWNS.** Not "describe MCP servers" but: **when one design's component consumes another design's MCP server, that is a seam, and reflow2 already has `link-projects`, `seam_report` and `cap:seam-incompatibility` for exactly that.** The MCP-specific part is only that the contract can be READ from the server rather than typed by hand. ⚠️ Counter: reading a live server is network I/O, which the gates deliberately do not do — `reflow2_check` says so in as many words about an artifact at a URL.

═══ THE FLO2 HALF, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT CLAIM ═══

*"I think the flo2 project will need both."* — both the many-client transport AND the API-engineering practice.

⚠️ **THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT FLO2, WHICH IS A SEPARATE PROJECT WITH ITS OWN GRAPH AND ITS OWN OWNERS.** AGENTS.md rule 6 and `dec:central-host`'s own repo-boundary note both apply: nothing may be built into flo2 from here without his word, and what flo2 needs is flo2's design to record. What reflow2 can decide alone is whether it OFFERS something flo2 could consume.

📌 **BUT THE TRANSPORT HALF IS ALREADY ANSWERED AND WORTH SAYING PLAINLY:** if flo2 is a web app whose users have no CLI, it is an MCP client over HTTP by construction — which is the `dec:central-host` option (b)/(c) ground, where the transport is built and the missing pieces are authentication and attribution. **The second half — the contract description — is the genuinely unbuilt one.**
properties.name: OPEN — MCP has no OpenAPI equivalent, and reflow2's Interface vocabulary is that shape; is describing an MCP surface a product opportunity or a distraction?
properties.rationale:
Kept separate from `dec:central-host` because that node is about WHERE reflow2 runs and who can reach it, while this is about whether an MCP surface can be DESCRIBED — two questions that happen to have arrived in one message. The transport half of his message was folded into that node as new evidence; only this half needed a new question.

Option (c) is recorded with the strongest objection this project has rather than as an opportunity, because "reflow2 could also do X" is precisely the reasoning that turns a design brain into a tracker, and the same argument already killed the Task node type on 2026-08-25.

Option (d) is marked as promising because it reframes the idea onto ground reflow2 already owns — seams between linked designs — rather than claiming a new category. Its counter is specific and may be fatal: reading a live server is network I/O, and the gates deliberately do none.
